convention: literal line-by-line, as in batch H02's brief
reasoning_summary:
Sapphic and Alcaic enjambment (e.g. 1.9.3-4 gelu...acuto, 1.10.7-8 iocoso...furto, 1.12.59-60 parum castis...lucis) left as split fragments with agreement explained in notes, never words moved across lines.
Tmesis (1.9.14 quem...cumque, 1.16.2 quem...cumque) rendered 'whatever/whichever' in place and noted.
Negatives kept where they stand: 1.9.15 nec (governing sperne in 1.9.16), 1.13.13 non (governing speres), 1.13.18 nec (governing solvet), 1.16.5-7 anaphoric non.
Metaphors literal with meaning noted: carpe diem 'pluck the day', reseces 'cut back' (pruning), macerer 'I am steeped', mala avi 'with evil bird' (omen), the ship-allegory of 1.14.
1.12.3-4 recinet...nomen imago kept as 'whose will re-echo, playful, / name the image', imago = echo noted.
Textual doubts noted: 1.12.46 Marcelli (vs emended Marcellis), 1.12.21 punctuation of proeliis audax (source's stop followed).
1.15 Nereus' prophecy: source's opening quotation mark kept with a note; no closing mark in source, noted at 1.15.36.
Supplied possessives ('his', 'your') marked in notes; Greek-form names kept as persons (Atridae, Laertiades as 'son of Laertes', Tydides as 'son of Tydeus') with notes.
